text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malaysia and Indonesia decide to refer their claims on the Sipadan and Ligitan islands to International Court of Justice.
- Taiwan and Hongkong protesters break through Japanese maritime cordon to land on disputed Diaoyu/Senkaku islands and plant Taiwanese and Chinese flags.
- Seven Umno candidates disqualified from contesting party elections for abuse of power and flouting party rules.
- Market analysts say property buyers become highly price-sensitive.
- Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau arrests two men in connection with Amcol Holdings' aborted multi-million-dollar project in Mauritius.
- Garment exporter Easyknit International Holdings becomes the second initial public offering to close at Hongkong $2.90 on its trading debut, 15 cents below its $3.05 issue price.
- Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew says Singapore has to deregulate its system quickly or be 'wiped out in five to seven years'.
- Commercial property transactions in the first nine months of this year totalled about Singapore $9 billion.
- Cafe-bakery chain Delifrance launches initial public offer of 45.16 million shares at Singapore 78 cents each, first French company in Singapore do so.
- Talk of restructuring of Hong Leong group and possible listing of Quek Leng Chan's Hongkong financial services arm, Guoco Group in Kuala Lumpur listing boosts speculative activity.
- U.S. $600 million joint venture airline proposed by Singapore and India may be hit by the new government's policy to be announced next month.
